answer: Divergent-Commitment Registry. Each identity must commit to a unique trajectory through a shared search space: agents publish successive signed answers at a fixed inlet, and the registry rejects any two identities whose answer sequences remain identical across a karst of held-out probes. Because clones cannot diverge without revealing independent reasoning, an attacker must run and staff each clone separately past a ridge of probe epochs, paying full compute and operator cost per identity rather than copying one state.
